record.paper_title: The Quest for Equational Axiomatizations of Parallel Composition: Status and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Auxiliary operators for CCS parallel composition
record.original_question: Does there exist one binary auxiliary operator that preserves bisimulation equivalence and whose addition to the recursion-free fragment of CCS is sufficient to obtain a finite equational axiomatization of the parallel composition operator? Equivalently, prove or refute the conjecture that no single binary operation can finitely axiomatize parallel composition up to bisimulation, so that two auxiliary operators such as left merge and communication merge are necessary.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the recursion-free fragment of Milner's Calculus of Communicating Systems (CCS), built from the constants 0 (inaction) and the action prefixes a. (for a in a given set of actions Act including a complementation involution and a silent action τ), with binary operators + (nondeterministic choice) and ∥ (parallel composition / merge), interpreted operationally by the usual structural operational semantics and compared modulo strong bisimulation equivalence. It is known (Bergstra–Klop) that adding the two binary auxiliary operators "left merge" ⌊ and "communication merge" ∣ yields a finite, sound and ground-complete equational axiomatization of bisimilarity. It is also known (Moller) that no finite equational axiomatization of ∥ exists over the pure recursion-free CCS signature modulo bisimilarity, and (Aceto et al.) that Hennessy's single binary merge does not yield such a finite axiomatization either.

Question: Does there exist a single binary operator f, definable by a set of structural operational semantics rules so that bisimilarity is a congruence with respect to f, such that the equational theory of bisimilarity over the recursion-free fragment of CCS enriched with f admits a finite, sound, and ground-complete equational axiomatization (in particular, finitely axiomatizing the parallel composition ∥)?

Equivalently, prove or refute the conjecture that no such single binary auxiliary operator exists, so that at least two auxiliary binary operators (such as left merge and communication merge) are necessary for a finite equational axiomatization of parallel composition modulo bisimilarity.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is not yet resolved in full generality, but significant partial progress has been made. Aceto, Castiglioni, Fokkink, Ingolfsdottir, and Luttik (CSL 2021; ACM TOCL 2022; arXiv:2010.01943) formulate three natural assumptions on the SOS rules of an auxiliary binary operator and prove that no operator satisfying all three assumptions can yield a finite ground-complete axiomatisation of bisimilarity over recursion-free CCS. The general question for arbitrary single binary auxiliary operators (without those assumptions) remains open.

status_evidence.title: Are Two Binary Operators Necessary to Obtain a Finite Axiomatisation of Parallel Composition?
status_evidence.snippet: Proves that no auxiliary binary operator satisfying three natural assumptions on its SOS rules can enable a finite axiomatisation of bisimilarity over recursion-free CCS.
status_evidence.claim: The single-operator conjecture is confirmed under three natural assumptions, indicating partial resolution.

status_evidence.title: Are Two Binary Operators Necessary to Finitely Axiomatise Parallel Composition? (CSL 2021)
status_evidence.snippet: Conference version establishing the impossibility result under stated operational assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial negative result toward the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: CCS with Hennessy's Merge has no Finite Equational Axiomatization
status_evidence.snippet: Aceto et al. show that Hennessy's single binary merge does not yield a finite axiomatization.
status_evidence.claim: A specific candidate single binary operator is ruled out.
